notes: Re-adjudicated by kb/Work PB5844, on the contingency kb/Work PB5373 class 3 named ("re-adjudicate if a method for the clause is ever provided"), and corrected by the branch's review R1-1. §1985:VII.2.8.4 GR6 asks that for an external file connector "all RECORD DELIMITER clauses in the run unit which are associated with that file connector must have the same specifications". Two written clauses therefore agree only when they write the same arm: STANDARD-1 (declined as a reel-device element, §1985:I.1.5.2.5.1, but still the specification the entry writes) disagrees with each implementor-name, and BINARY-SEQUENTIAL and LINE-SEQUENTIAL disagree with each other (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-149, DOC-A.1-150). An entry that writes no clause is no RECORD DELIMITER clause and agrees with every arm (kb/Work PB5311). The relation, ExternalDescriptor.RecordDelimitersAgree, is checked for every pair of entries at compile time (ExternalFileConnectorRules.Check, COBOL6847, citing this rule at --std 85) and at run time (EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH). The 1985 refusal pb5844_rd_external_specs_differ_85 (STANDARD-1 in one program, BINARY-SEQUENTIAL in the other) is refused with COBOL6847; pb5311-external-reserve-and-delimiter-defaults (an omitted clause beside STANDARD-1) compiles and runs. retired-witness: conformance-test:DocumentedNonSupportWitnessTests.RecordDelimiterFeatureName_NamedNonSupportWarning_PinnedToSpec (kb/Work PB5844 provides the implementor-names, so the test that pinned the feature-name arm's COBOL1778 decline is deleted)
